run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-17T07:10:02Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on service frontend is explained by frontend's own error spans: HTTP 500 on GET /api/data caused by 'connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080' (the ad Service ClusterIP) and HTTP 500 on POST /api/checkout caused by 'dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused' (the payment Service ClusterIP). Frontend error spans were zero at every step through 07:09:02Z, became non-zero at 07:10:02Z, peaked at 401.05 per 10m at 07:17:02Z, and read 0 again at 07:26:02Z. Both dependencies had just been restarted: Deployment ad and Deployment payment each rolled a new ReplicaSet at 2026-11-17T07:08:28Z whose only pod-template difference is the annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt (same image, env and resources); the old pods were killed at 07:08:31Z and 07:08:32Z and the new pods started at 07:08:30-07:08:31Z. During cold start the new ad and payment containers were CPU-throttled in 89-93% and 90-97% of CFS periods (07:09-07:15Z), versus 4-21% for their predecessors; Service ad emitted no spans at all in the windows ending 07:15:02Z and 07:17:02Z and its container logged requests only from 07:17:24Z, while Service payment's charge-span volume dipped to 72.8 and 94.3 per 5m before recovering, its container logging only successful 'Transaction complete.' charges from 07:16:29Z. The supported mechanism is transport-level unavailability of the restarted ad and payment pods surfaced as connection-refused 500s at frontend; what issued the 07:08:28Z rollout restart is not observable, and the flagd fault flags adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100% in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config remain a hypothesis because the failure path they declare does not match the transport refusals observed.

claims.text: In frontend, spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR were 0 at every 10-minute-increase step through 07:09:02Z and became non-zero at the 07:10:02Z step (12.63 per 10m on GET /api/data and on client span grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, 9.47 on POST /api/checkout and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder); the GET /api/data and AdService/GetAds error series peaked at 401.05 per 10m at 07:17:02Z-07:18:02Z and read 0 again at 07:26:02Z.

The frontend failures were HTTP 500 responses on GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout whose child client spans grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds and grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder carry otel.status_code ERROR; the sampled error traces cover 07:09:25-07:09:36Z.

Exact diagnostic text on the failing frontend spans: 'executing api route (pages) /api/data' logs '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 100.65.180.246:8080', and 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout' logs '13 INTERNAL: failed to charge card: could not charge the card: rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 100.70.188.60:8080: connect: connection refused"'.

The refused addresses are the Service ClusterIPs of the two dependencies: Service ad is 100.65.180.246 port 8080 targetPort 8080 (selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad) and Service payment is 100.70.188.60 port 8080 targetPort 8080 (selector opentelemetry.io/name=payment).

Deployment ad and Deployment payment were rolled out at 2026-11-17T07:08:28Z: their new ReplicaSets ad-6cb57f76d and payment-9c8ffb665 were created 07:08:28Z with pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt=2026-11-17T07:08:28Z, and their templates are otherwise identical to the previous ReplicaSets ad-554b849958 and payment-55766d76b9 (same image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad and 2.1.3-payment, same env, same resources).

The rollout sequence in otel-demo: Deployment ad 'Scaled up replica set ad-6cb57f76d from 0 to 1' at 07:08:28Z and old pod ad-554b849958-mbnxm 'Stopping container ad' at 07:08:31Z; Deployment payment scaled up payment-9c8ffb665 at 07:08:28Z and killed payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb at 07:08:32Z; new pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 were Scheduled 07:08:28Z, Created and Started 07:08:30-07:08:31Z. No OOMKilled, Evicted, Failed or Unhealthy events appear for these pods.
At query time pods ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 and payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 are Running with container ready=true and restartCount 0, both with startTime 2026-11-17T07:08:28Z.

The new containers were CPU-throttled almost continuously during startup: pod ad-6cb57f76d-xmcq6 throttled-period ratio was 0.89-0.93 from 07:09:02Z to 07:14:02Z (0.71 at 07:15:02Z, 0.34 at 07:17:02Z), and pod payment-9c8ffb665-qrm84 was 0.90-0.97 from 07:09:02Z to 07:11:02Z (0.75 at 07:12:02Z, 0.37 at 07:13:02Z); their predecessors ad-554b849958-mbnxm and payment-55766d76b9-c4wgb ran at only 0.04-0.19. CPU usage of the new pods was 0.073-0.098 cores (ad) and 0.030-0.040 cores (payment) versus 0.006-0.012 and 0.012-0.015 for the old pods.

Service ad produced no spans at all in the windows ending 07:15:02Z and 07:17:02Z (5-minute increases 0, after 493.3 at 07:09:02Z, 332.2 at 07:11:02Z and 91.5 at 07:13:02Z), and had recovered to 214.0 at 07:19:02Z; its container logged normal 'Targeted ad request received' and 'Non-targeted ad request received' lines from 07:17:24Z onward with no error lines.

Service payment's charge span volume fell from about 165-180 per 5m to 72.8 at 07:12:02Z and 94.3 at 07:14:02Z and recovered to 162.2 at 07:16:02Z; its container's retained log lines (593 in the queried window) span 07:16:29Z-07:17:57Z and consist only of paired 'Charge request received.' and 'Transaction complete.' lines.

In the 2-minute per-service error-span increases across 06:40-07:20Z, only frontend (121.3, 337.7, 309.3, 202.7 in successive windows from 07:10:02Z) and frontend-proxy (58.7, 173.3, 161.3, 114.7, 6.7) show a large burst; checkout shows 5.9 in the window ending 07:11:02Z, and payment, cart and accounting show 0 throughout.

Deployment ad and Deployment payment declare container port 8080 and FLAGD_HOST=flagd/FLAGD_PORT=8013, with resources limits cpu 50m/memory 450Mi (ad) and limits cpu 20m/memory 160Mi (payment); all 21 deployments in otel-demo carry explicit CPU requests and limits, so a CPU limit is not unique to these two workloads.

The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config, read at 07:29Z after the incident window, contains fault-declaring flags with adFailure defaultVariant 'on' (description 'Fail ad service', state ENABLED) and paymentFailure defaultVariant '100%' (description 'Fail payment service charge requests n%', state ENABLED); paymentUnreachable is 'off'.

After the outage the two dependencies behaved normally and the app-level faults declared by the flags were not visible: ad logged only normal targeted and non-targeted ad responses from 07:17:24Z, and payment logged a charge/'Transaction complete.' pair for every request from 07:16:29Z-07:17:57Z with no failed charge, while the ConfigMap read later still declares adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100%.

payment recorded zero error spans over the whole 06:40-07:20Z range, and ad's own error series shows only 1.33 per 2m at 06:52:02Z before the incident, so the failing operations are visible on the callers' client spans, not as failing server operations on the dependencies themselves.

A pod crash, OOM kill or eviction of ad/payment is rejected as the cause of the outage: the only otel-demo events for these objects are the rollout Scale-up/Scale-down, Pod Killing, Scheduled, Pulled, Created and Started events, and both resulting pods are Running with restartCount 0.

A failure of checkout's own charge logic is rejected as the source of the checkout 500s: the frontend span text is a transport dial error to the payment ClusterIP 100.70.188.60:8080 ('connect: connection refused'), and payment logged successful transactions once reachable.

Best-supported remaining explanation for the alert: cold start of the newly created ad and payment pods under their tight CPU limits (throttled 89-97% of CFS periods for 6+ minutes) left port 8080 of those single-replica Services not listening, so frontend and checkout TCP connects were refused, producing frontend HTTP 500s on GET /api/data and POST /api/checkout and the RequestErrorRate alert.

Candidate not confirmed: the fault-injection flags adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100% in ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config name exactly the two dependencies that failed and could be what prompted restarting Deployment ad and Deployment payment at 07:08:28Z, but the observed failure path is TCP connection refused (ad received zero requests during the outage) rather than in-service failures, so it is kept as a hypothesis.

The 07:08:28Z rollout restart was issued externally (pod-template annotation kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt) by an operator or chaos tool; no object currently in the cluster identifies the actor or its reason.

Add startupProbe/readinessProbe to the ad and payment containers (both currently declare livenessProbe null and readinessProbe null, so a started-but-not-listening container is immediately treated as ready) and raise their cold-start CPU budget so a restart does not leave the single-replica Service refusing connections for minutes.

Use the cluster audit log to identify who ran the rollout restart on Deployment ad and Deployment payment at 2026-11-17T07:08:28Z, and confirm whether the flagd flags adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100% were intended and whether the running 2.1.3 services actually evaluate them.

The ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config was read at 07:29Z, after the incident window, so flag values during 07:08-07:17Z are unverified.

flagd health during the window is unknown: fetch_pod_logs on flagd-56d9c6c679-xwgx9 for 07:00-07:26Z returned status no_data with 0 lines from all three containers, so flag reloads or flagd unavailability cannot be excluded.

The alerting rule RequestErrorRate was not returned: list_prometheus_rules returned status no_data in view e982dcb2-3d8a-4fc3-a273-d8a17dd6c5b8-t1:200850a2-5be6-4c0c-83db-eb163563f811, so the rule expression and the alert annotation value 2.5777777777777775 could not be verified.

frontend and checkout application logs did not corroborate the span evidence: frontend log view 6ec89d75-e81c-4139-98a0-a73a2010cae4-t0:bee5ae67-f4ab-4c74-86fb-38042294b99f returned status no_data with 0 lines, and checkout log view e1d37860-79ec-407f-83b4-abfe10a8a01b-t2:40338129-8522-4e44-9688-7cdfdb7552c6 returned status no_data with 0 matching lines from 2666 lines read.

The NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned no_data (view e7e2b225-77fe-4eb6-b0fe-08fceb78daed-t3:1c1d55c4-6af0-4685-8ccb-0482cf6f27c0); whether any policy existed during the incident and could have contributed to refused connections is unknown, since an empty current result is not proof of absence.

Trace evidence is a biased sample: the sampled error spans in view e982dcb2-3d8a-4fc3-a273-d8a17dd6c5b8-t0:51350480-088f-4a85-a9dd-f7f07c608642 are truncated and cover only 07:09:25-07:09:36Z; ad and payment log views are also incomplete (newest 60 of 276 lines and newest 100 of 593 lines), span counts are not unique request counts, and no complete call graph or failure-rate figure is available.
Node-level CPU pressure on node i-0e9f8b08cc290a884, which hosts both restarted pods, was not measured, so a node-side contribution to the slow cold start cannot be excluded or confirmed.
next_steps: Pull the Kubernetes audit log for 2026-11-17T07:08:00-07:09:00Z to identify the principal that issued the rollout restart on deployments ad and payment and any accompanying ConfigMap update.

Compare the delivered flagd-config demo.flagd.json with the chart's default values to confirm whether adFailure=on and paymentFailure=100% were deliberately injected, and check the ad and payment service versions for whether those flags are actually evaluated.
Add startup and readiness probes plus a higher cold-start CPU allocation for ad and payment, then rehearse a single-replica restart during business traffic to measure time-to-listening.
Review whether ERROR and alerting baselines exist for the ad and payment Services themselves, since their own error metrics stayed at zero while their callers failed on connection refused.
